statement: Managed split and merge workflow ownership survives process failure: both coordinators claim durable ownership through the existing claimDurableWorkflow/assertTransitionFence machinery (no longer process-local), source acknowledgements carry fence tokens and stale-fenced acks are rejected with a typed outcome, participant transitions follow an explicit graph, and sibling promotion lands after or inside the epoch flip — an abort on one node can never interleave with a cutover on another. doneWhen: the test-receipt probe reads solve/evidence/workflow-fencing-wiring.receipt.json with outstanding 0 — claim-wiring, fenced-ack, stale-fence-rejection, and participant-graph receipts all passing.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Wire the EXISTING durable-workflow-storage-ownership.js claim/fence-token/lease/assertTransitionFence into both coordinators (the schema-provisioning-job-owner path is the working precedent); do not invent a parallel ownership or fencing concept.

Every source acknowledgement carries a fence token; fence validation stops being opt-in for split/merge acks, and a stale-fenced ack is rejected with a typed STALE_FENCE outcome (never silently applied).
Each new regression test must fail when the corresponding claim/fence/graph mechanism is reverted while the rest of the change remains.

The oracle evidence files must be written by a deterministic evidence harness that re-runs the recorded proof commands (focused test files, red-on-revert checks) at quest terminal; no hand-authored metric values.
